name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is noted specifically as a Levite in Nehemiah 10:9 and was among those who sealed the covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27. His identification as a Levite places him within the tribe set apart for religious duties in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'Yahweh has reckoned,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 10:11, indicates a personal identity connected to the Lord's sovereign counting or accounting.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hashabiah as a descendant of Levi, aligning him with the priestly tribe. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite who participated in the covenant renewal ceremony documented in Nehemiah 10. His inclusion among the signatories highlights the Levites' involvement in upholding Israel's commitment to God's law during the post-exilic restoration. This underscores the importance of faithful service and covenant fidelity among God's chosen tribe of priests.
